key_insight: LASKO treats skill editing as a structured geometric control problem, using a Lie algebroid anchor and bracket to separate visible Markdown changes from latent noncommuting edit structure.
engineering_relevance: This provides a fast screening layer for agent self-improvement pipelines, helping systems reject low-value or order-sensitive edits before paying for expensive LLM validation.
method: Model typed, anchored Markdown skills as the base space.
Represent edit policies as sections of a controlled Lie algebroid with anchor ρ.
Use Lie-bracket tests to detect noncommuting edit interactions before rollout/validation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary benchmark results, including nearly 15× speedup on a causal extraction task versus brute-force validation with a DeepSeek V3.1 4-bit 671B model.
watch_item: The benchmark evidence is preliminary, so the practical gains may depend on how well the geometric abstraction matches real skill-edit workflows and validation costs.
paper_title: Agentic Skill Optimization over Lie Algebroids
